introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2024. Additional Mathematics 2 (code 0575), Paper 2. Duration: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions, questions 1 to 8). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions, questions 9 to 11; if this section is chosen, Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (answer any two questions, questions 12 to 14; if this section is chosen, Section B may not be chosen). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
14. (i) Two events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A)=\dfrac45$, $P(B)=\dfrac34$, $P(A\cap B)=\dfrac23$.

Find

a) $P(A\cup B)$. *[3 marks]*
themes: probability of unions and intersections of events
tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)

questions.corrige_markdown:
By De Morgan's law, $A'\cap B'=(A\cup B)'$, so

$$P(A'\cap B')=1-P(A\cup B)=1-\frac{53}{60}=\frac7{60}.$$

**Answer: $P(A'\cap B')=\dfrac7{60}$.**
themes: probability of unions and intersections of events

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) A basket contains $20$ white and $40$ green cups. It is observed that $40\%$ of the white cups and $30\%$ of the green cups are breakable. A cup $X$ is selected at random from the basket. Find the probability that

a) $X$ is breakable. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Number of cups: $20+40=60$.

Breakable white cups: $40\%$ of $20=8$. Breakable green cups: $30\%$ of $40=12$. Total breakable: $8+12=20$.

$$P(\text{breakable})=\frac{20}{60}=\frac13.$$

(Equivalently $\frac{20}{60}\times0.4+\frac{40}{60}\times0.3=\frac{2}{15}+\frac15=\frac13$.)

**Answer: $\dfrac13$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) $X$ is a green cup or breakable. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$P(G\cup B)=P(G)+P(B)-P(G\cap B)$, where $G$ = green and $B$ = breakable.

- $P(G)=\dfrac{40}{60}$;
- $P(B)=\dfrac{20}{60}$;
- $P(G\cap B)=\dfrac{12}{60}$ (green and breakable).

$$P(G\cup B)=\frac{40+20-12}{60}=\frac{48}{60}=\frac45.$$

(Check: the cups that are neither green nor breakable are the $12$ unbreakable white ones, $\frac{12}{60}=\frac15$, and $1-\frac15=\frac45$.)

**Answer: $\dfrac45$.**
themes: probability of unions and intersections of events

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) $X$ is a white cup given that it is breakable. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$$P(W\mid B)=\frac{P(W\cap B)}{P(B)}=\frac{8/60}{20/60}=\frac{8}{20}=\frac25.$$

(Of the $20$ breakable cups, $8$ are white.)

**Answer: $\dfrac25$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)
